title: Investigation of pathogenesis of the symptom gingival bleeding in patients with hemophilia A and B
summary: Gingival bleeding in idividuals with hemophilia A or B often is related to the impairment of hemostasis. In this study gingival bleeding of people with hemophilia is compared to people of the same sex, age, smoking habit, and periodontal diagnosis but without hemophilia.

interventions.name:
Patients with hemophilia A or B
Periodontal examination (plaque index, probing pocket depth, recessions). Gingival bleeding will be assessed and compared as bleeding on probing (BOP) and gingival bleeding index (GBI). Hematological examination (blood sample at arm vein and analysis for factor VIII

Individuals without hemophilia A or B that are matched to the case group according to sex, age (±5 years), nicotine consumption (active smoker/non-smoker), tooth number (±2 teeth), and periodontal diagnosis.
Periodontal examination (plaque index, probing pocket depth, recessions). Gingival bleeding

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- written informed consent
- Test (patients): hemophilia A or B
  Control (probands): no heritary bleeding disorders or medication that interfer with hemostasis
Exclusion criteria:
- disease or condition (e.g., heart valve prothesis) that requires antibiotic prophylaxis for measures (assessment of periodontal probing parameters) causing transitory bacteriemia
- additional bleeding disorder
- intake of drugs that interfere with hemostasis (e.g., ASS)
